picks.title: Tencent Music’s MusicBuddy combines AI music creation, editing, distribution and promotion
picks.excerpt: Tencent Music is testing MusicBuddy, an AI platform that pairs song generation with a multitrack editor driven by natural-language chat, then pushes tracks to release and promotion.
picks.rationale: A new end-to-end tool from a major streaming platform: generation, a chat-driven multitrack editor, distribution and promotion in one workflow, which signals where creator tooling is heading.

picks.title: Using AI To Make Patches For The Yamaha CS-80 Synthesizer
picks.excerpt: A Jose's Vintage Keys video shows Anthropic's Claude programming patches on a MIDI-modded Yamaha CS-80, turning text descriptions into sound-design starting points on vintage hardware.
picks.rationale: A hands-on sound-design workflow you can copy: an LLM drives a vintage analog synth over MIDI to turn text descriptions into patches. It differs from the 09-18 DX7 plain-English tool in both hardware and method.

picks.title: Instagram adds AI songs to DMs
picks.excerpt: Instagram is testing a Meta AI song-creation option in the DM inbox: users add lyrics and pick a genre to generate a track to send to friends, echoing Snapchat's paid Chat-to-Song.
picks.rationale: A new Instagram feature brings AI song generation to a mass-market messaging app. It is Meta's own release, separate from Snapchat's 09-23 Chat to Song.

picks.title: LiveSynth: A Streaming Neural Synthesizer for Instrument Cloning and Text-to-Instrument
picks.excerpt: LiveSynth is a streaming neural synthesizer that clones an instrument's timbre zero-shot from a reference recording or generates one from a text prompt, and plays in real time rather than rendering audio offline.
picks.rationale: Producer-facing research: a neural instrument that clones a timbre zero-shot or builds one from text, and plays in real time instead of rendering offline.

picks.title: ‘Suno is the new auto-tune’: Meet the artists using AI to go viral
picks.excerpt: Dazed profiles masked TikTok-viral acts such as Kilo Kent and Zemi who sing their own songs and run the vocals through Suno like a studio effect, arguing the songwriting stays theirs.
picks.rationale: A creator-workflow angle not covered before: artists write and sing their own songs, then use Suno as a vocal effect, much like auto-tune, to go viral.

alternates.title: MIRA: A Musical Intent Refinement Agent for Aligning Text-to-Music Generation with User Intent
alternates.excerpt: MIRA is an agent that refines underspecified text-to-music prompts toward the user's implicit intent on instrumentation, structure, rhythm and mood, instead of relying on a single global text-audio relevance score.
alternates.rationale: Prompt-refinement agent for text-to-music; useful but a second arXiv card would crowd the five.

alternates.title: Audiotool reveals six winners from its ‘Let’s Build!’ hackathon
alternates.excerpt: Audiotool's music-app hackathon winners include Pocket Producer, an AI agent for music producers, and an AI A&R Assistant that analyses tracks and estimates earning potential, alongside DAW-conversion and sheet-music tools.
alternates.rationale: Prototype AI producer and A&R tools from a hackathon; new but early-stage.

alternates.title: Lalu's Corner: Who Controls the Digital Version of You?
alternates.excerpt: A column on artist likeness in the AI era: the Jason Isbell suit alleging Suno's name block is bypassed by spacing letters, a deadmau5 deepfake endorsement, and the Jorja Smith soundalike, plus how labels split between licensing and takedowns.
alternates.rationale: Opinion column on likeness rights; commentary rather than a new event.

dedup.note: Dropped as repeats: Hypebot 'DistroKid Takedown Wave Hits Indie Artists After UMG Lawsuit' is extra reporting on the same DistroKid takedowns published 10-11 (theverge.com/entertainment/1009309), with no new filing, ruling or policy. MusicRadar's Sony deepfake-takedown story is the same 260,000+ figure published 10-06 (MBW). Dropped as commentary or low-signal: the Kraftwerk Karl Bartos interview (AI is a side topic) and Olivia Rodrigo's AI stance (a celebrity quote with no new event). The Hypebot Lalu's Corner column, MIRA (arXiv) and Audiotool's hackathon went to alternates. The five picks come from five different outlets. No clusters were present in the pool.
